answers.answer: At the September 25, 2026 cutoff, owner Lina authorizes offline CSV plus optional local JSON reports (DEC-203) for downstream offline analysis. DEC-201 chose offline operation because operators work in a disconnected warehouse office. The documented command is `oriole compare left.csv right.csv --output report.csv`; JSON command syntax is not supplied. Inputs are read-only, output must not overwrite either input, and source exports must be retained until a reviewer accepts or rejects the report. Preserve left-export field order, followed by right-only fields in their original order. Reports support human investigation. The contributor browser/hosted viewer proposal and local mockup do not establish approved hosted scope: the viewer remains unapproved. No delivery date, production rollout, or telemetry system was approved. This is a documented workflow, not evidence of live execution.

The current repository batch size is 125 rows (batch_rows: 125), consistent with the September 25 update. This replaces the September 21 observation of 200 rows; 100 rows was only an unapproved draft suggestion. Separately, no running installation was observed and no running installation configuration is supplied. Repository settings and the tiny local synthetic unit test establish neither deployed batch size nor a production installation, representative warehouse coverage, or an accepted end-user report.

As of September 25, SAMPLE-201 is closed: the owner and test maintainer update records creation of a synthetic fixture containing one item at two locations and a passing duplicate-location comparison, test D201. This supersedes its September 16 open status but does not establish broad coverage or live behavior. ENC-202 remains separately open because an approved non-ASCII location sample is still needed. Next, request that sample from the test maintainer and record encoding-test evidence independently. Neither D201, the earlier tiny local unit test, nor the reviewer key example closes ENC-202.

DEC-202 requires the composite key (item_id, location_id), treating both components as opaque strings and preserving case and leading zeros. Do not normalize identifiers numerically, fold case, match on item alone, or automatically deduplicate repeated item identifiers. These rules prevent loss of identifier distinctions and accidental merging of separate locations or records: item "0042" at location "a" is distinct from "42" at "A". They supersede the draft numeric-matching suggestion and remain in force after DEC-203.

Blank or missing quantities mean unknown/missing evidence, not zero; the draft blank-to-zero suggestion was superseded. The tool has no authority to alter either input ledger: inputs are read-only, reports must not overwrite them, and exports must be preserved during review rather than rewritten to make comparisons pass. A discrepancy report neither authorizes warehouse corrections nor establishes which ledger is financially authoritative. Missing records may also reflect filtered exports rather than deletion.

No person is established as the approver of warehouse ledger corrections. The September 16 records explicitly leave that authority unidentified, and the latest September 25 update confirms it remains unidentified. Lina approves tool-design/output scope, but that role does not establish authority to approve warehouse ledger changes; report output grants no such authority.

answers.answer: As of the latest evidence, September 25, 2026, DEC-101 requires manual pilot publication with `wrangler pages deploy dist` and optional CI. Owner Mira approved it September 8 so the operator reviews every artifact. Automatic Git publication and mandatory CI remain deferred until release frequency warrants their setup. The September 20 demonstration does not supersede this: integration only might have been enabled, the screenshot is missing, and no new owner approval exists. Confirm settings before a real release; the demonstration establishes neither deployed revision nor publication path. September 25 reaffirms DEC-101, contradicting notes/release.md.

The checked-in timeout is 45 seconds, matching the September 25 change from 60 to 45. The September 21 value of 60 is superseded for repository configuration. No production timeout is established: no production rollout or runtime observation accompanies the changes, the sample-17 receipt is staging-only, and no production receipt or runtime configuration export is supplied. The earlier 30-second value was a design proposal; notes/status.md does not substantiate its production claim.

Only REST-101 is closed. The September 25 operator update reports that a disposable volume was allocated with its sparse-file flag preserved and the synthetic restore exercise passed that day, citing receipt restore-25. That report supports closure; a separate receipt artifact is not supplied. CAL-102 remains blocked by the missing leading-zero sensor identifier in the calibration sample. Next: ask the test maintainer for an approved synthetic sample containing it. A written procedure alone does not resolve the blocker. The latest update contradicts notes/status.md claiming both are complete.

The restore fixture is `./data files/pilot.db`. Preserve its sparse-file flag when allocating the test volume, or quota estimates will be wrong. Consult the storage maintainer before reserving the volume. The September 22 uncommitted operator note explicitly retains this constraint after allocation or a successful restore for future exercises. The September 25 completion records preservation of the flag and does not retire the constraint.

No. Mira's DEC-102 permits only approved sample manuals; public/customer uploads and external ingestion are not approved. An external manual is not eligible simply because it is available. Document rights and update ownership must be agreed before expanding the approved sources. This is an approval boundary; the records do not establish a technical ingestion block. It survives publication-process changes and is explicitly reaffirmed September 25. The blanket approval in notes/boundaries.md conflicts with the owner decision and latest update.

No production on-call owner is assigned in the supplied records as of September 25, 2026. Escalation staffing remains open, and Mira's owner role does not automatically make her the on-call contact. The claim in notes/status.md that Mira is on-call conflicts with the operator work list and latest update. No live access is supplied to establish a later assignment.

September 25 explicitly preserves this policy. Automatic Git publication and mandatory CI remain deferred proposals, to revisit if release frequency justifies setup. The September 20 suggestion that Git integration might have been enabled lacks its screenshot and any superseding owner decision: it establishes neither approval nor the production publication path or deployed revision. Confirm settings before a real release. Keep reviews tied to the actual artifact revision and retain the previous accepted artifact until replacement acceptance.

The repository timeout is 45 seconds in config/service.yaml, corroborated by September 25's change from 60 to 45. The working note's 30 seconds is stale and September 21's 60 seconds is superseded. The running production timeout is unknown: no production rollout or runtime observation accompanies the change, and no production receipt or runtime configuration export is supplied. A local build and the staging-only sample-17 preview do not establish production configuration.

At the September 25 cutoff, REST-101 is closed. The update reports allocation of the disposable volume with its sparse-file flag preserved and a successful synthetic restore exercise on September 25, citing receipt restore-25. The supplied evidence is that report and receipt identifier, not a separate receipt artifact; it supports a synthetic exercise, not a production restore. Older allocation-blocked notes are superseded. CAL-102 remains blocked by the missing leading-zero sensor identifier sample. Ask the test maintainer for an approved synthetic sample. The restore completion closes only REST-101; writing a procedure does not resolve the calibration blocker.

Preserve the restore fixture path `./data files/pilot.db`, including its space, and its sparse-file flag when allocating the test volume; otherwise quota estimates are wrong. Consult the storage maintainer before reserving the volume. The September 22 uncommitted operator note explicitly retains this constraint after allocation or a successful restore, so September 25's successful exercise does not retire it.

Only approved sample equipment manuals are authorized for the pilot under Mira's DEC-102. Public/customer uploads and external ingestion are not approved. Reports do not authorize warehouse corrections or establish financial ledger authority. The hosted viewer remains unapproved; the contributor mockup does not establish service approval. No delivery date, production rollout or telemetry system was approved in the supplied records. DEC-203 supersedes CSV-only output while preserving DEC-202 semantics.

The current checked-in batch limit is 125 rows, set by config/report.yaml and corroborated by the September 25 update. This supersedes the September 21 observation of 200 rows; the earlier 100-row suggestion was unapproved. No batch limit is established for a running installation: no installation configuration is supplied and no running installation was observed. Repository configuration and a tiny local unit test do not establish deployed behavior.

SAMPLE-201 is closed: the September 25 owner and test maintainer update records creation of the synthetic duplicate-location fixture and a passing comparison, test D201. Closure is supported by that recorded update; no separate D201 test artifact is supplied, and this does not establish representative warehouse coverage or production acceptance. ENC-202 remains open. Its next action is to request an approved non-ASCII location sample from the test maintainer. Passing the duplicate-location case cannot close this separate encoding work item.

DEC-202 requires matching the pair (item_id, location_id) as opaque strings, preserving case and leading zeros in both identifiers. Item-only matching can merge records belonging to different locations; numeric matching can collapse distinct identifiers such as 0042 and 42. Duplicate item identifiers may represent separate locations and must not be automatically deduplicated. The uncommitted review note illustrates that item "0042" at location "a" differs from item "42" at location "A"; the authoritative rule is Lina's DEC-202, explicitly retained by the September 25 update.

A blank quantity means unknown or missing evidence, not zero, under DEC-202, retained by the September 25 update. A discrepancy report cannot authorize changes to source exports: inputs are read-only, output must not overwrite them, and exports must be retained until review acceptance or rejection. Reports support investigation and neither select an authoritative ledger nor approve corrections. Review acceptance is not established as permission to rewrite source exports.

The authorized approver for actual warehouse ledger corrections is unidentified in the supplied records, explicitly reaffirmed at the September 25 cutoff. Lina's tool-design role does not establish warehouse correction authority, and tool output does not approve corrections. No person can therefore be named as an authorized correction approver on this evidence.

answers.answer: As of the latest supplied evidence, September 25, 2026, DEC-101 requires manual publication using `wrangler pages deploy dist`, with optional CI. Owner Mira approved this on September 8 so the operator reviews every artifact. Automatic Git publication and mandatory CI remain deferred until release frequency justifies setup. The September 20 demonstration changes neither approval nor policy: integration only might have been enabled, the screenshot is missing, and no superseding owner decision exists. It establishes neither deployed revision nor publication path; confirm settings before a real release. September 25 explicitly reaffirms DEC-101.

The checked-in timeout is 45 seconds, matching the September 25 change from 60 to 45. The 30-second working note is stale, and September 21's 60-second configuration is superseded. Production timeout is not established: no production rollout or runtime observation accompanies the changes, no production receipt or runtime configuration export is supplied, and the staging-only sample-17 preview receipt cannot establish the running pilot site's timeout.

REST-101 is closed: the September 25 operator update records allocation of a disposable volume with its sparse-file flag preserved and a passing synthetic restore exercise that day, receipt restore-25. This report supports closure; the receipt itself is not separately supplied. CAL-102 remains blocked by the missing leading-zero sensor identifier in the calibration sample. Next action: ask the test maintainer for an approved synthetic sample. Older notes saying REST-101 awaits a volume are superseded; a procedure alone did not resolve either blocker.

The fixture is `./data files/pilot.db`. Preserve its sparse-file flag when allocating the test volume, otherwise quota estimates are wrong; consult the storage maintainer before reserving the volume. The September 22 uncommitted operator note explicitly says this constraint survives allocation and successful restore, so future exercises must retain it despite REST-101's September 25 closure.

No. Mira's DEC-102 permits only approved sample manuals; public/customer uploads and external ingestion are not approved. External manuals cannot be ingested merely because they are available. Expansion requires agreement on document rights and update ownership; no such agreement is supplied. This source boundary survives publication-process changes and is reaffirmed September 25. The Git demonstration supplies no authorization to expand it.
No production on-call owner is assigned in the supplied records as of September 25, 2026. Escalation contact remains an open staffing question, not Mira's automatic role as approving owner.

Owner Mira approved this in September 8 DEC-101 so the operator reviews every artifact, and September 25 reaffirmed it. Automatic Git publication and mandatory CI remain deferred proposals, to revisit if release frequency justifies setup; their proposed rationale was reduced repetition and artifact/source traceability. The September 20 claim that Git integration might have been enabled lacks its screenshot and proves neither settings nor publication path. Possible implementation is not approval. Confirm settings before release and reconcile any automation with the manual policy. Reviews must remain tied to artifact revisions; rebuilds require fresh review, and retain the previous accepted artifact until its replacement is accepted.

The repository timeout is 45 seconds, matching the September 25 change from 60. The running production timeout is unknown: no production rollout receipt, runtime configuration export, or runtime observation is supplied. September 21 records a successful local build, the then-current 60-second repository setting, and a staging-only preview receipt for sample-17; none establishes the production revision or timeout. The earlier 30-second timeout was only a design proposal.

REST-101 is closed as of September 25: the operator update records allocation of the disposable volume with its sparse-file flag preserved and a passed synthetic restore exercise, citing receipt restore-25. This resolves the September 15 allocation blocker. The supplied evidence is that report and receipt identifier, not a separate receipt file or proof of a production restore. CAL-102 remains separately blocked because the calibration sample lacks a leading-zero sensor identifier. Ask the test maintainer for an approved synthetic sample. Writing a procedure does not resolve the missing-sample blocker, and REST-101's closure does not close CAL-102.

Preserve the restore fixture path `./data files/pilot.db` and its sparse-file flag when allocating the test volume; otherwise quota estimates will be wrong. Consult the storage maintainer before reserving the volume. This constraint is recorded in the September 22 uncommitted operator note and remains applicable to future exercises even after allocation and the successful September 25 restore.

Only approved sample manuals are authorized under Mira's September 8 DEC-102, reaffirmed September 25. The records do not enumerate individual approved manuals or providers. Public/customer uploads and external ingestion are not approved. Document rights and update ownership must be agreed before expanding sources; the supplied evidence does not establish that prerequisite has been resolved. Publication-process changes do not relax this restriction. Equipment specifications remain upstream.

No production on-call owner is assigned in the supplied records through September 25. Coverage and escalation assignment remain an open staffing question; Mira's owner role does not automatically make her the escalation contact. The restore fixture is `./data files/pilot.db`; quote this path in shell commands. Preserve its sparse-file flag when allocating the test volume, or quota estimates will be wrong. Ask the storage maintainer before reserving the volume, request allocation, then run and record the exercise. These constraints survive completed allocation and a successful restore and still apply to future exercises.

No. Mira's September 8 DEC-102 permits approved sample manuals only; public/customer uploads and external ingestion, including external manuals outside the approved set, are not approved.
